title-group.article-title: IL-2 drives Foxp3 expression in CD4+ T cells

abstract.title: Abstract
abstract.p: Interleukin-2 (IL-2) signalling through STAT5 is required for regulatory T cell identity. Here we show that IL-2 induces Foxp3 in naïve CD4+ T cells.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) depend on IL-2 for survival1,2. TGF-β also contributes (Smith et al., 2020).

sec.title: Results
sec.p: We first asked whether IL-2 alone is sufficient.

sec.title: IL-2 induces Foxp3 in a dose-dependent manner
sec.p: Treatment with 10–100 U/ml IL-2 increased the frequency of Foxp3+ cells from 2% to 35% (Fig. 1A), while IFN-γ levels were unchanged. CD8+ T cells did not respond.

caption.title: IL-2 induces Foxp3.
caption.p: (A) Frequency of Foxp3+ cells after 72 h with IL-2 (mean ± SD, n = 3). CO2 was 5%.

sec.title: STAT5 is required
sec.p: Blocking STAT5 with an inhibitor abolished the effect; data are available at example.org/data.

sec.title: Cell culture
sec.p: Cells were cultured at 37°C in RPMI-1640.

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: IL-2 is sufficient to induce Foxp3 in vitro; its role in vivo remains to be tested [2–4].
